newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela cabinet approves electricity rate scheme.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela cabinet approves electricity rate scheme.

text.p: Venezuela's cabinet of economic ministers on Friday approved a framework to govern electricity tariff increases, though higher rates will not begin to be phased in until May, a government official said on Friday.
"We reviewed the new scheme presented by the Electricity Regulatory Commission (CREE), and we have recommended that it be applied," Vice Planning Minister Armando Leon told reporters.
Exact rate rises will be determined next week, though the increases would go into effect only after President Rafael Caldera gives the final approval.

Electricidad de Caracas has long pressed for a rise in tariffs. Government sources told Reuters in March the company had asked for an average 40 percent rise, based on an 85 percent increase for domestic customers and 25 percent for commercial users.
The sources said technicians at the commission considered the utility's request too high.
Market analysts have said they expect an average increase of between 15 and 20 percent for the company.
